item.title: Lions plan to have Brian Branch, Cade Mays in lineup this week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Lions got safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays back at practice a couple of weeks ago and both players are set to return to the lineup in Week 7.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions got safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays back at practice a couple of weeks ago and both players are set to return to the lineup in Week 7.

Head coach Dan Campbell said on Monday that the expectation is that Branch and Mays will play against the Packers. Branch tore his Achilles last season and Mays broke his wrist over the summer.

"Barring anything negatively happening between now and the game, we plan on playing both of those guys," Campbell said on Monday.

The Lions will need to formally activate both players and they made space for them by placing three players on injured reserve during their bye week.

item.title: Andy Dalton tells Eagles "no thanks," will sign with another team soon
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With starting quarterback Jalen Hurts out indefinitely, the Eagles have had to scramble to fill out the depth chart.
item.content:encoded:
With starting quarterback Jalen Hurts out indefinitely, the Eagles have had to scramble to fill out the depth chart.

Tanner McKee started on Sunday against the Panthers. They also have rookie Cole Payton, and they added Joe Milton from the Cowboys' practice squad.

They had 16-year veteran Andy Dalton, but the Eagles cut him nine days ago. They wanted to bring him back, but Dalton has politely declined, we're told.

Dalton, who has played for the Bengals, Cowboys, Bears, Saints, Panthers, and Eagles, will be signing with a team other than the Eagles as soon as tomorrow. And his arrival in a new city likely will trigger a current member of the quarterback room making his exit.

Which would then, frankly, make that player a potential option for the Eagles.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes ties Tom Brady for fewest games to 100 QB wins
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Patrick Mahomes has done a lot of winning in his career.
item.content:encoded:
Patrick Mahomes has done a lot of winning in his career.

The Chiefs' victory over the Chargers on Sunday was Mahomes' 100th regular-season win as a starting quarterback in 131 games. That puts him in a tie with Tom Brady for fewest games started for 100 victories.

What does Mahomes think of that feat?

“My honest first reaction is they've said this from 97 on. I'm like, ‘When did Tom lose another game?’ Because I feel every game I win, I tie him,” Mahomes said with a laugh in his postgame press conference. “But in all seriousness, it's always an honor to be in any conversation as far as winning football with him. That's the GOAT. He knows how to win football better than anyone really in any other sport. And so, if you can be mentioned in any category with him, it's special.

“As I've gone throughout my career, I think I've gotten better and better at winning. You know, it's not always pretty. It's not always how I want it to be. I want to throw three touchdowns, four touchdowns, and I want to put up big stats but whenever your defense is playing like they are today, you can't force it. And after I forced that one early in the game, I just said, ‘Hey, let's figure out the best way to win the football game,’ and we were able to do that.”

Mahomes added that being on these kinds of lists with Brady does give him motivation, but he also knows surpassing Brady on most of them is “still so far away.”

“I mean, there's so many more games I have to win and Super Bowls and all that different type of stuff,” Mahomes said. “All I can focus on is today and winning today and then moving on to the Seahawks this next week. I mean, [Brady], he's got 15 more years. I'm only 30. I'm 31. He's played to 45. So, that's a long way away.

“But, like I said, it's always an honor to be in any conversation with him and the way he played the game because that's how you want to play it. You want to be a competitor. You want to win and you want to bring your teammates along. And that's who I want to be as my career goes on.”

item.title: Foster Moreau and Bhayshul Tuten have two TD catches each as Texans lead Jaguars
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Tuten also had a rushing touchdown overturned on a bad holding call.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten has reached the end zone three times today, but only two of his touchdowns counted. Texans tight end Foster Moreau also has two touchdowns today, and a Texans field goal on top of it gives Houston a 17-14 lead at halftime.

A Tuten touchdown run was overturned on a bad holding call early in the game, a major error by the official that was particularly costly when the Jaguars came away with no points after a Trevor Lawrence interception on the same possession.

But in the second quarter, Tuten left no doubt when he caught two short Trevor Lawrence passes and scored on both of them. On the first, he winded his way through the Texans' defense for a 27-yard touchdown. The second was easy, as the Texans left him open on second-and-goal for a two-yard touchdown.

The Texans' passing game is also making plays. Texans wide receiver Jaylin Noel has two catches, one for 50 yards and one for 34 yards. Texans wide receiver Nico Collins burned Travis Hunter for a 42-yard gain, and later drew a pass interference penalty on Hunter in the end zone to give the Texans first-and-goal at the 1-yard line. Texans wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. made his first catch as a Texan, a 14-yarder over the middle in the second quarter.

But while the wide receivers are getting the big plays, it's the tight end, Moreau, who is getting into the end zone. He has two touchdown catches, one from six yards out and one from one yard out.

The Texans have a couple of big injury concerns on defense, as linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair is being evaluated for a concussion, and safety Reed Blankenship was carted to the locker room late in the second quarter.

It's been a tight, back-and-forth game with major implications for the AFC South.

item.title: Assistant GM Ed Dodds will run Colts personnel department for rest of the season
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Colts fired General Manager Chris Ballard on Monday and they have named an interim head of their personnel department through the end of the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts fired General Manager Chris Ballard on Monday and they have named an interim head of their personnel department through the end of the 2026 season.

The team said, via multiple reporters, that assistant GM Ed Dodds will take over those responsibilities. Head coach Shane Steichen and the rest of the staff outside of the personnel department will report to ownership under the interim arrangement.

Dodds has been in his current role since 2018 and he joined the Colts shortly after Ballard was initially hired in 2017. He has interviewed for GM openings with several teams in recent years.

One of the first orders of business for Dodds to deal with is the November 10 trade deadline. With the 1-5 Colts starting to look to 2027, there will likely be calls from other teams trying to pluck players from their roster and the Colts will have to decide how many pieces they're willing to part with in exchange for assets that can help a new regime try to build a winner in the future.

item.title: Colts opt for a half-measure, for now
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both coach Shane Steichen and G.M.
item.content:encoded:
In January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put both coach Shane Steichen and G.M. Chris Ballard on clear notice that things had to improve in 2026. Sunday's loss to the previously-winless Titans shows that not nearly enough improvement has been made.

And now the Colts are 2-4. After last year's 8-2 start, they're 3-12.

In lieu of firing both Steichen and Ballard, Irsay-Gordon opted to make the move that will have the lesser impact on the team's ability to try to turn it around. There's no clear option on the roster to take over as interim head coach. Unless the team goes off the board (like it did when bringing in Jeff Saturday four years ago), it would be hard to make an interim hire that could try to move the Colts into position to win the AFC South.

They'll still need to stabilize the front office, which currently is laying the foundation for the offseason plans in 2027. Those plans, however, will change once the Colts hire a new G.M. — who, if the eventual G.M. is currently working for another team, will carry into the building impressions and strategies regarding the players to target in free agency and the draft.

The first order of business will be to hire a new coach, unless Steichen turns it around. The job becomes more attractive if the new G.M. has a clean slate. Every G.M. has a personal list of coaches with whom the G.M. would like to partner. Unless the next G.M. coincidentally has "Steichen, Shane" at the top of that list, the half-measure (for now) eventually will become a full overhaul of the organization.

Anything less than a playoff appearance will result in that overhaul. The only hope for the 2026 Colts will come from the firing of Ballard lighting a fire.

The first chance to show some spark comes in six days, when the Colts visit the 5-0 Vikings in Minnesota.

item.title: Rams have fallen to fifth-best odds to win the Super Bowl
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Rams entered the season as overwhelming favorites to win the Super Bowl.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams entered the season as overwhelming favorites to win the Super Bowl. After starting the season 2-4, their odds have fallen.

But they may not have fallen as far as some would expect for a team that just lost at home to the Cardinals: The Rams still have the fifth-best odds to win the Super Bowl, at +1000.

The four teams ahead of the Rams are the 49ers at +580, the Bills at +720, the Chiefs at +850 and the Ravens at +900.

Despite their shockingly bad start to the season, bettors and bookmakers still think the Rams have one of the best rosters in the NFL, with a team that should be playing very good football down the stretch. Making the playoffs is no sure thing after this start, but if the Rams do make it, there's every reason to believe they'll be a tough team to beat.

item.title: Aaron Glenn: No confusion about who got the ball to start the second half
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's on-field interview before the start of the second half on Sunday went viral, but Glenn said on Monday that his comments were misinterpreted.
item.content:encoded:
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's on-field interview before the start of the second half on Sunday went viral, but Glenn said on Monday that his comments were misinterpreted.

Glenn told Aditi Kinkhabwala of CBS that the team would be ready to go despite being down 17-3 and that "the good thing is we get the ball, we get a chance to go move it and finish." That was widely interpreted to be Glenn saying that the Jets would receive the kickoff to start the second half, which was not the case, and Glenn said on Monday that he was talking about what would happen after the defense forced a stop.

“No, I actually talked about just the offense,” Glenn said on Monday, via Howie Kussoy of the New York Post. “I think they were talking about sustaining drives, and my conversation with them is when the offense gets the ball back, man, we want to be able to sustain a drive and go score. Then when the defense gets back on, we want to make sure we stop them and get the ball back to our offense. That’s what I was talking about when it comes to that. The conversation was talking about the offense at that time.”

Things actually did work out as Glenn hoped as the Jets forced a punt and then scored on a touchdown pass to rookie wideout Omar Cooper. They would eventually pull within 17-13, but the Patriots went on to win 26-19.

item.title: Josh Allen on flicked TD pass to Keon Coleman: "I was just trying to make a play"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Midway through the third quarter of Sunday's victory over the Raiders, Bills quarterback Josh Allen made another signature play for a touchdown pass.
item.content:encoded:
Midway through the third quarter of Sunday's victory over the Raiders, Bills quarterback Josh Allen made another signature play for a touchdown pass.

It was third-and-8 when Allen was pressured, moved to his left, then sent a backhand flip about 15 yards into the end zone to an open Keon Coleman, who made the catch for the score.

It's nothing new for Allen, who has been an improvising playmaker for years now.

"It's who he is," head coach Joe Brady said in his postgame press conference.

Allen noted that he saw Coleman flash open, but it was the crowd — that was full of Bills fans — that really indicated the play's success.

"[O]nce it comes out, you kind of get hit and tumble around, and it's so hard in these away games, which feel like home games, once you hear the crowd go crazy, you're like, 'I don't know if it's a touchdown, I don't know if it's an interception,’” Allen said. "So again, he finds himself in the right place at the right time and finds a way to get open.”

Before Allen flicked it to Coleman, there was a moment where it looked like he could run.

"Again, I was just trying to make a play,” Allen said. “They played really good defense. I stepped up in the pocket, felt somebody coming from the left side there, stepped back, and again, quick eyes, saw our guy open and gave him a chance.”

For his part, Coleman said he was just trying to find space where Allen could see him and he wasn’t surprised by the result.

“I watched it, I was right there. I saw him flicking like that,” Coleman said. “I might have robbed Skyler [Bell]. He appeared behind me. He thought that ball was coming in when I just came out north. I just saw him in trouble, bro. Trying to make a play.

“He threw it around the dude. It's just him, bro.”

That’s just part of the experience of playing with Allen.

“Play [is] never dead until the whistle blows,” Coleman said. “With him, even if a guy comes free hard to get him down — you might get there, but attacking him is a whole different obstacle. So, my job is when I feel that's going on, you have to get your eyes back to the quarterback and find what we're doing."

item.title: Jalen Hurts has deep vein thrombosis, multiple pulmonary embolisms
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Eagles QB most likely will not play again this season.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 season of Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is most likely over.

Hurts, who played eight days ago with a blood clot in his leg, has been diagnosed with a deep vein thrombosis and a pulmonary embolism in each lung.

A pulmonary embolism is a very serious health condition. From the Mayo Clinic's website: "A pulmonary embolism can be life-threatening. About one-third of people with an undiagnosed and untreated pulmonary embolism don't survive."

The Eagles and agent Nicole Lynn issued a statement on Monday morning disclosing the change in Hurts's condition.

"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts," the statement explains. "In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition.

"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. 'blood thinners'). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.

"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.

"We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."

It's good that a serious health condition is being taken seriously. There's still a very real question as to whether it was taken as seriously as it should have been from the outset.

We'll have some more thoughts on that later. For now, we wish Jalen the best as he focuses on resolving a serious health condition.

item.title: Colts fire GM Chris Ballard
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Ballard was in his 10th season with the team.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts have made a major change in the wake of Sunday's loss to the Titans.

Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon announced that they have fired General Manager Chris Ballard. Ballard had been in the job since 2017 and made the playoffs twice in his first four seasons, but have not been back since 2020 while cycling through a number of different quarterbacks.

That led Irsay-Gordon to say this offseason that improvement was needed, but Sunday's loss dropped the Colts to 1-5 on the season and became the final act of his tenure.

"I am grateful to Chris for his years of service to the Colts and for everything he poured into this organization," Irsay-Gordon said in a statement. "He cared deeply about our team and our community, and we wish Chris and his family all the best. As I said at the start of the season, the sense of urgency has never been higher. Our standard is to compete for championships, and I believe a change in leadership is necessary to meet that standard. Making this change during the season was a deliberate decision. Waiting would only delay the important work that needs to begin now. We will conduct a thorough search for our next general manager and take the time necessary to identify the right leader for the future of this organization. I also want to be clear: this decision does not change our goals for the season. We have a lot of football in front of us, and I expect us to compete, improve, and win football games."

Head coach Shane Steichen remains on the job, but he's clearly on thin ice moving forward with Ballard already gone.

item.title: Bills hold off Raiders 33-30 to move to 5-1
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Bills quarterbcak Josh Allen was 23-of-33 for 255 yards and two touchdowns.
item.content:encoded:
The Raiders hung with the Bills. The game was tied 13-13 at halftime and 23-23 in the fourth quarter.

It never felt like the Bills were in danger of losing, though the Raiders never went away.

Josh Allen led Buffalo to a 33-30 win in Las Vegas as the Bills moved to 5-1. The Raiders fell to 3-3.

The Bills gained 345 yards, with 169 coming in the second half when they scored 20 points.

Allen was 23-of-33 for 255 yards and two touchdowns, including a Houdini-esque 12-yard touchdown pass to Keon Coleman on third-and-8 in the fourth quarter.

James Cook's 3-yard touchdown run with 4:43 left was the go-ahead score, with Tyler Bass adding a 38-yard field goal with 1:56 remaining.

Bass also made kicks from 44, 28 and 47.

Coleman caught four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown, and Cook had 22 carries for 95 yards and a touchdown.

The Raiders made it interesting on Kirk Cousins' 44-yard touchdown throw to Tre Tucker with 1:32 left.

The Raiders, though, didn't have a prayer of recovering the onside kick, something they haven't done since 2017 against the Chiefs. Matt Gay kicked a drop kick too far, and Khalil Shakir caught it in the air.

Cousins finished 23-of-41 for 313 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. Tucker had five catches for 97 yards and two touchdowns, and Michael Mayer added seven receptions for 95 yards.

item.title: Rams K Blake Grupe left SoFi Stadium with crutches and a brace on his leg
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Rams signed kicker Blake Grupe after Week 5.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams signed kicker Blake Grupe after Week 5. They'll be signing another kicker after Week 6.

Via Arash Markazi of The Sporting Tribune, Grupe left SoFi Stadium with his leg in a brace and on crutches. It was a result of Grupe's effort to make a tackle on a kickoff return.

The attempt took courage, especially since he's listed at 5-7 and 156 pounds. (Which could mean he's actually shorter and lighter than that.)

Either way, the hit will apparently end Grupe's time with the Rams. The next question is whether they'll bring back Harrison Mevis or look elsewhere for help.

And that's far from the biggest of the problems the Rams have. They're 2-4 after six games, and they're getting closer and closer to having too many losses to qualify for the postseason.

Can they heat up? Yes. Will they? We'll find out, one game at a time.

item.title: Caleb Williams "just let it rip" in his return from hamstring tear
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Caleb Williams had one question for the media as he made his way into the tunnel toward the visiting locker room.
item.content:encoded:
Caleb Williams had one question for the media as he made his way into the tunnel toward the visiting locker room.

"Y’all like that?" Williams asked rhetorically, smiling, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN.

The Bears quarterback returned after missing three games with a torn hamstring. He completed his first 12 passes and finished 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a touchdown.

"I felt confident from the jump," Williams said. "When I get out there, I'm going to feel confident in my leg, in myself and in my guys and the O-line. So I just let it rip, let these guys go make plays for us, get first downs and score touchdowns."

The Bears now have a quick turnaround, with a Thursday night game against the Patriots looming.

Despite four sacks, Williams said he is no worse for wear in his first game back.

"Felt great to get hit after three weeks of just rehabbing," Williams said. "So [I] feel strong, feel good. Obviously got to go and take care of it this week. It's going to be a weekly thing, just taking care of it, staying up to date on it and taking care of my body."

item.title: Bengals put Tanner Hudson on IR
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals have opened up a spot on their 53-man roster as they return from their bye week.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals have opened up a spot on their 53-man roster as they return from their bye week.

They announced that tight end Tanner Hudson has been placed on injured reserve. Hudson's agent announced last week that Hudson will miss the rest of the season after he tore his pectoral in Week 5.

Hudson had seven catches for 33 yards, including a touchdown in Cincinnati's Week 5 win over the Dolphins. Hudson is in his fourth season with the Bengals and his eighth season as an NFL player.

Mike Gesicki, Erick All, Drew Sample, and Jack Endries are the team’s remaining tight ends. They could add to that number whenever they decide to fill the opening Hudson leaves on the roster.

item.title: Steelers pull out 26-19 win over Bucs in overtime
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Aaron Rodgers threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Germie Bernard for the game-winner in overtime.
item.content:encoded:
Nothing was going right for the Steelers on Sunday. They trailed the Buccaneers 16-3 in the fourth quarter.

Pittsburgh won 26-19 in overtime.

The Steelers are 4-2 and the Bucs 1-5.

The Steelers dominated the fourth quarter, gaining 230 yards and forcing two Jalon Daniels interceptions. Their fourth-quarter scoring drives were 68, 24, 37 and 2 yards.

Chris Boswell's 58-yard field goal tied the game 16-16 with 1:55 left. Two plays later, former Bucs cornerback Jamel Dean intercepted Daniels. Dean went 40 yards with the return of the errant pass before Daniels pushed him out of bounds at the Tampa Bay 3.

The Steelers couldn't get it into the end zone, but Boswell's 20-yard kick with 1:21 left gave the Steelers their first lead.

They left too much time for the Bucs, though, as Tampa Bay needed only a field goal to send the game to overtime.

With eight seconds left, Chase McLaughlin kicked a 53-yard field goal to tie it 19-19. It was McLaughlin's fourth field goal of the day, with the others from 43, 47 and 52 yards.

The Steelers got the overtime kickoff, and Aaron Rodgers got his seventh overtime win with a 12-play, 70-yard drive that burned 6:45 of the 10-minute period. He threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Germie Bernard for the game-winner.

The Bucs drove across midfield, but on fourth-and-8 with 1:06 remaining, Jalen Ramsey sacked Daniels to end it. Ramsey had two sacks as did Nate Herbig.

The Bucs sacked Rodgers five times and frustrated him for most of the game. But he finished 33-of-49 for 253 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. DK Metcalf caught 11 passes for 93 yards, and Bernard had 11 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown.

The Steelers outgained the Bucs 300 to 224.

Daniels was 22-of-43 for 164 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions.

item.title: Giants put J.J. McCarthy in with Saints up 34-10 in fourth quarter
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: It's J.J.
item.content:encoded:
It's J.J. McCarthy time for the Giants for the rest of the day.

After the Saints turned Jameis Winston's second interception of the day into a 34-10 lead, the Giants pulled their starting quarterback and replaced him with McCarthy. McCarthy had been in for one snap to run the zone read in the first half, but this time he's actually playing quarterback.

McCarthy's first drive didn't end any better than Winston's final two, however. He was picked off by cornerback Martin Emerson, who also had one of the two interceptions off of Winston.

The Giants led Sunday's game 10-0, but the Saints have steamrolled them in the second half. We'll find out after the game if there's any chance of a lasting quarterback change for John Harbaugh's club.

item.title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson faces a potential suspension for spitting
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The ejection of Bills safety C.J.
item.content:encoded:
The ejection of Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for spitting on an opponent raises an interesting question, as it relates to the additional discipline to be imposed by the league office.

Last year, the NFL adopted a new approach to spitting. It now results in a one-game suspension, sort of.

It started when Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter spit on Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott before the first play from scrimmage in the regular-season opener. Because Carter's ejection covered the entire game, his punishment — a fine in the amount of a game check — simulated a suspension.

Later in the season, Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase spit on Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey. The officials didn't see it, so Chase wasn't ejected. Instead, he was suspended for the next game.

For Gardner-Johnson, the ejection caused him to miss half of the Week 6 game against the Raiders. Will he be suspended for another full game? Will the league fashion an NCAA-style targeting punishment that keeps him out for the first half of the Bills' next game?

Because Buffalo has a Week 7 bye, the clock isn't ticking as loudly as it ordinarily would be. Still, the league has a decision to make given the new precedent that was set in 2025, when the punishment for spitting morphed from a fine into a suspension. And Gardner-Johnson presents the first example of a player who missed roughly half of a game after being ejected.

item.title: Todd Monken wants to enjoy the win over the Ravens while he can
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In Week 1, the Browns were embarrassed by the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
In Week 1, the Browns were embarrassed by the Jaguars. Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin, quoting JuJu Smith-Schuster, declared on NBC, "The Browns is the Browns."

Since then, the Browns is 4-1.

The biggest win of the season came on Sunday, when the new Browns beat the old Browns to create a three-way tie atop the AFC North. Because the Browns have beaten both the Ravens and the Steelers, both of whom are 4-2, Cleveland is in first place.

And first-year head coach Todd Monken intends to relish it. Until tomorrow.

"I’m going to enjoy tonight," Monken told reporters after the 13-10 win. "And that’s what you have to do in the NFL. These are the nights that you don’t ever want to end, because tomorrow it’s on to the next game. And so, I sit there, I know it sounds really goofy, but you sit there in bed and you don’t want the night to end. It’s 10:30 and you’re tired as hell and you want to be up another 15, 20, 30 minutes to enjoy it, because, shit, tomorrow I’ve got to look at the offensive tape and then you’ve got to move on to the next game."

The next game could push the Browns to 5-2; they head to Tennessee to play the Titans. And the Browns are road favorites.

The best news is that the Browns are relevant. They'll likely be jockeying for a playoff berth after Thanksgiving.

In a league littered with teams that claim they want to win the Super Bowl, the truth is that they hope to still be in the mix after the fourth Thursday in November. Because that's when the NFL season truly starts.

This year, the Browns will likely be one of the teams that is hoping to finish strong enough to earn a spot in the AFC playoff field, and to win as many games as they can once the single-elimination phase commences.

item.title: Jameis Winston: I'd love to put myself in a better position to execute
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Giants quarterback Jameis Winston spent the fourth quarter of Sunday's game watching J.J.
item.content:encoded:
Giants quarterback Jameis Winston spent the fourth quarter of Sunday's game watching J.J. McCarthy try to pull off an improbable comeback and the day ended without any certainty that he'd be back on the field in Week 7.

Head coach John Harbaugh said the immediate aftermath of a 34-27 loss to the Saints was not the time to make an announcement about a starter moving forward. Winston threw a touchdown as the Giants moved to a 10-0 lead in the first quarter, but he was pulled after 34 straight Saints points and a pair of second-half interceptions.

McCarthy led the Giants to 17 points and had a shot to tie the game on the final drive, which made his argument for getting the start next week pretty straightforward. Winston was asked what he'd say to Harbaugh about his case.

"That's him. You know, that's the decision that he'll have to make," Winston said, via a transcript from the team. "What I would love is to just put myself in a better position to execute. And that just starts with me. Things that I can control, going out there every single play, doing my very best."

McCarthy has only been with the Giants for a few weeks, but they traded for him so that they had an option other than Winston as they played out the season in the wake of Jaxson Dart's knee injury. That option looked like a viable one on Sunday and his time as a starter is likely coming even if he isn't on the field for the first snap in Houston next Sunday.

item.title: Falcons signing Andy Dalton, cutting Cooper Rush
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Falcons are making a change in their quarterback room.
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons are making a change in their quarterback room.

Andy Dalton is signing with Atlanta, and he'll take up the roster spot the Falcons will open up by cutting Cooper Rush, according to multiple reports.

As PFT reported Sunday, Dalton was offered a contract by the Eagles, but he turned them down to sign elsewhere today. Now we know that elsewhere is Atlanta.

The 38-year-old Dalton was traded from Carolina to Philadelphia in March and played in one game for the Eagles, throwing an interception while Jalen Hurts was being checked with a concussion. The Eagles cut him shortly after that, but when Hurts had to go on injured reserve with a blood clot, they wanted Dalton back. Dalton had other offers.

The best offer came from the Falcons, who have already played four quarterbacks this year: Rush, Michael Penix, Jack Strand and Tua Tagovailoa. If Penix stays healthy, Dalton will stay on the sideline, but that's a pretty big "if," and Dalton may just become the fifth quarterback to play for the Falcons this season.

item.title: Brian Schottenheimer: Cowboys' effort and fight is right, but mistakes are killing us
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Cowboys fell to 2-4 with Sunday night's loss to the Packers.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer defended his team's effort but not the results after Sunday night's loss to the Packers.

On a night when Dak Prescott threw two interceptions, Schottenheimer pointed the finger at turnovers.

"The effort is right, the fight is right, but mistakes are killing us," Schottenheimer said. "We've got to protect the football."

At 2-4, the Cowboys are not a good team right now, but there are no good teams in the NFC East and the Cowboys are actually the betting favorites to win the division. Schottenheimer thinks there's still a future for his team.

"We're in a hole. We've put ourselves there. There's one way out of it. I told our guys we've got to work, we've got to find solutions, we can't repeat mistakes. And they understand that," Schottenheimer said.

Although Schottenheimer defended Prescott's effort, he made clear that he wasn't happy about the interceptions.

"The ball matters more than anything in the National Football League," Schottenheimer said. "It's the ball. Second, it's the line of scrimmage. And we haven't been very good in the last two games, so that's what we're responsible and accountable for, and I stand up here and accept that."

item.title: Davante Adams suffered non-contact leg injury late in Sunday's loss to Cardinals
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: If Adams misses time, Rams become thin (again) at receiver position.
item.content:encoded:
The slumping Rams may be scrambling to find help at receiver.

Veteran Davante Adams suffered a non-contact injury to his left leg late in the game. He pulled up when running into the end zone on a pass route, reached for his left knee, and hobbled off the field for attention.

The Rams had only one more offensive play, a go-ahead touchdown that did not last.

Coach Sean McVay wasn't asked about Adams's apparent injury during the post-game press conference.

Last year, Adams missed the final three games of the regular season with a hamstring injury (and still led the NFL in touchdown catches).

For the season, Adams has 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns. The bulk of the production came in Week 2 vs. the Giants (195 yards) and Week 3 at the Broncos (137). In the other four games combined, he has 148 total receiving yards.

Still, they need him. Puka Nacua, who missed the two games (hip/groin/pre-hernia) in which Adams went off, is their top target in the passing game. On Sunday, Nacua had six catches for 80 yards, including three for 62 on the Rams' final drive of the game.

Beyond Nacua and Adams, the Rams have Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, C.J. Daniels, and Alex Bachman at receiver. They may need to find someone else, depending on whether and to what extent Adams will miss time.

The question becomes whether they're willing to eff them picks in an effort to acquire a receiver via trade before the deadline arrives in 22 days. And the situation will invite even more scrutiny of the decision to invest their bonus first-round pick from last year's trade with the Falcons on a quarterback and not a receiver — especially since it was obvious that they don't have much depth behind Nacua and Adams.

item.title: Bears DB Kyler Gordon: Return to lineup was "everything I wanted"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bears defensive back Kyler Gordon's lack of availability over the last two years has been a source of frustration for the Bears and his return to the lineup on Sunday illustrated why the team has missed him so much.
item.content:encoded:
Bears defensive back Kyler Gordon's lack of availability over the last two years has been a source of frustration for the Bears and his return to the lineup on Sunday illustrated why the team has missed him so much.

Gordon had three sacks and two forced fumbles, including a strip-sack of Falcons quarterback Michael Penix late in the fourth quarter that allowed the Bears to run out the clock on a 31-23 victory. He's the second Bears defensive back to record three sacks in a game and the second defensive back for any team with at least three sacks and two forced fumbles in the same game.

Gordon missed the first five games of the season and all of the summer while working his way back from a calf injury that limited him to five appearances in 2025. After the game, he called the return "everything I wanted."

"I wanted to be on the field and contribute, add to this team and help the direction we're going to go, and that's what I did," Gordon said, via the team's website.

No one will be expecting weekly repeats of Sunday's exploits, but the Bears will be banking on Gordon staying in the lineup and working to make their defense better as they try to build on their 4-2 start to the season.

item.title: Kyren Williams: Offensive inconsistency "probably because I'm not out there"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Sunday's 18-16 home loss to the Cardinals dropped the Rams to 2-4 and continued a start that has many people scratching their heads given how high the hopes were for the team heading into the season.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday's 18-16 home loss to the Cardinals dropped the Rams to 2-4 and continued a start that has many people scratching their heads given how high the hopes were for the team heading into the season.

Everyone associated with the team is fielding questions about why things have gone so poorly, including running back Kyren Williams. Williams was asked about why he thinks the offense has been inconsistent from drive to drive over the first six weeks and he pointed to his role in his answer.

“I can’t tell you, bro,” Williams said, via Adam Grosbard of the Orange County Register. “Probably because I’m not out there.”

Williams played 70 percent of the snaps in the first five games and he outsnapped Blake Corum 42-16 on Sunday while fielding 13 touches to 11 for Corum. Williams' workload is in line with last season, but down from its peak in 2024 and he's seeing fewer carries than at any point since he became a starter. He was asked if he'd like to see that change in the coming weeks.

“I can’t really call that. It’s not on me,” Williams said. “But I just think no matter what, we gotta continue to have the energy. You gotta continue to, when plays are made, be excited, be happy so we uplift not only the offense but the defense and the special teams and just being able to have that camaraderie to where we’re playing off of each other and I think that’s what is going to allow us to be where we want to be.”

Musing about playing time and soul-searching about how to get into a groove weren't the kinds of things people expected from the Rams this season, but that's what happens when losses start to pile up and the Rams need to get right in a hurry if they want to avoid those things becoming the most consistent part of their season.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh on Mike McDaniel: We'll look at everything, offense needs to be addressed
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: McDaniel could be dismissed as offensive coordinator after an 0-6 start.
item.content:encoded:
The Chargers failed to score a touchdown in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs and they head into their bye week under increased speculation about whether offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will still be on the staff when they return in Week 8.

PFT reported "growing buzz" on Sunday that the Chargers will be parting ways with McDaniel after the team fell to 0-6 since putting him in charge of the offense. The Chargers have scored just 84 points in those six losses, which is a far cry from what many expected when McDaniel was hired to work with quarterback Justin Herbert in the offseason. Herbert threw his eighth interception on Sunday and has thrown at least one in each of the futile offensive performances.

After Sunday's loss, head coach Jim Harbaugh was asked if McDaniel will be calling the plays when the team returns against the Rams in two weeks.

"We're going to look at everything. . . . I feel bad for our players, our team, our coaches, our fans. And (the offense) needs to be addressed," Harbaugh said, via Noah Furtado of TheAthletic.com.

If the Chargers do make a move with McDaniel, former Jets head coach and current pass game specialist Adam Gase is expected to take over the offensive reins.

item.title: Last time the Chargers were 0-6, their QBs were Ryan Leaf, Moses Moreno and Jim Harbaugh
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Chargers are 0-6 for the first time since 2000.
item.content:encoded:
The Chargers are 0-6 for the first time since 2000. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh remembers that well.

That's because Harbaugh was one of the quarterbacks on the terrible 2000 Chargers, who were 0-6 through six weeks like this year's Chargers. That 2000 Chargers team ended the season 1-15.

The Chargers began the 2000 season with Ryan Leaf as their starting quarterback. Leaf had been the No. 2 overall pick in 1998, was awful as a rookie and missed all of his second season with a shoulder injury. The 2000 season was Leaf's last chance in San Diego, and it did not go well. Through the first two weeks, the Chargers were 0-2 and Leaf had one touchdown pass and five interceptions, so they benched him for Moses Moreno in Week 3.

Unfortunately, Moreno was also terrible, and he suffered a shoulder injury in that Week 3 game, so Leaf started again in Week 4. But after Leaf again struggled in Week 4, he was benched again, this time for Harbaugh.

Harbaugh started Week 5, and he completely transformed the Chargers' offense: Through the first five games, Moreno and Leaf had combined to average 131 passing yards, and totaled one touchdown pass and seven interceptions. In Week 5, Harbaugh threw for 348 yards, with two touchdowns and one interception, against the defending Super Bowl champion Rams. Unfortunately for the Chargers, their defense couldn't stop the Greatest Show on Turf, and the Rams won 57-31.

Harbaugh kept the starting job for four more games, but he didn't play as well, and by the time the Chargers were 0-10 they went back to Leaf to close out the season.

Leaf won one game as the starter, but the Chargers' 1-15 record was the worst in franchise history. At least, the worst so far. Harbaugh's 2026 Chargers have a chance to break the 2000 team's franchise record for the most losses in a season.

item.title: Chiefs stay unbeaten, Chargers stay winless
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Chiefs scored nine points on their first two possessions of Sunday's home game against the Chargers and that would be all they'd need to move their record to 5-0 on the season.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs scored nine points on their first two possessions of Sunday's home game against the Chargers and that would be all they'd need to move their record to 5-0 on the season.

Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert threw his eighth interception of the season, wide receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith lost a fumble and the Chiefs broke a three-game sackless streak by dropping Herbert four times in a 22-6 win. The loss drops the Chargers to 0-6 on the season and sends them into their bye week without any signs that things are getting better.

While there was plenty to like about the defensive effort on Sunday, the Chiefs probably won't be thrilled with the way the rest of the team performed in the second half of the game. They failed on a fourth down on their first possession of the third quarter and then saw punt returner Nikko Remigio lose a fumble to give the Chargers another chance. They forced another punt, but punted the ball back and then missed a field goal to allow the Chargers to hang around even as they did their best to give the game away.

Kenneth Walker ran for a pair of scores to help stake the team to a 19-3 halftime lead and is now up to eight in his first five games with the Chiefs. He finished the day with 128 yards on 19 carries while Patrick Mahomes was 23-of-30 for 272 yards. Those numbers would point to more scoring, but the missed kick and a Mahomes interception in the end zone in the first half contributed to the relatively modest output.

Mahomes completed passes to eight different receivers with Rashee Rice out of the game, which is a positive for the overall offensive depth in Kansas City moving forward. They did lose right tackle Jaylon Moore to a concussion during the game, which could be an issue when they head to Seattle for one of Week 7's marquee matchups.

The Chargers will not have to leave Los Angeles for their return to the field in Week 8, although they'll be the road team in their game against the Rams. Both teams have wildly underperformed expectations to this point in the season — the Cardinals have more wins at SoFi Stadium than the two tenants combined — and it will be interesting to see what kinds of changes the Chargers make during their bye week in an attempt to salvage something of what's already a lost season.

item.title: Cardinals stun Rams, defeat Los Angeles 18-16
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: A Super Bowl favorite to begin the season, the Rams have now fallen to 2-4 in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Maybe the Cardinals should only play at SoFi Stadium.

Arizona got its second win of the season on Sunday, stunning the Rams 18-16 for the club’s second victory of the season.

The first came Week 1 at the same venue over the Chargers.

Entering the week at No. 26 in yards allowed and No. 32 in points allowed, Arizona stifled Los Angeles’ offense throughout the contest.

The Rams barely had 100 yards at halftime with three three-and-outs. It didn’t help that the team lost its new kicker, Blake Grupe, to a knee injury early in the game when he made a tackle on a kickoff.

But the Cardinals were able to control the ball and the clock throughout the afternoon, winning time of possession 34:52 to 25:08. And while the club never reached the end zone, Chad Ryland was automatic in Rams territory with his six field goals — including his 43-yard make as time expired to give Arizona the win.

Los Angeles got to the end zone twice — once with Blake Corum’s 15-yard touchdown reception in the second quarter. It then took them until there were 47 seconds left on the clock for Matthew Stafford to find Colby Parkinson for a 6-yard touchdown. With Grupe out, punter Ethan Evans put the Rams ahead with a successful extra point.

But that lead did not hold, as Jacoby Brissett connected with Jalen Brooks for a 21-yard completion to open the ensuing Cardinals possession. An unnecessary roughness penalty tacked on 15 yards, putting Arizona in clear field goal range.

A few plays later, Ryland sent his sixth kick through the uprights for the win.

Brissett ended the day 24-of-35 passing for 218 yards with an interception. Trey McBride led with seven catches for 53 yards.

On the other side, Stafford finished 25-of-33 for 222 yards with two touchdowns. Puka Nacua had six receptions for 80 yards. Davante Adams — who hopped off the field late in the fourth quarter with an apparent leg injury — had three catches for 39 yards.

The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this season — two — than the Rams and Chargers, who have a combined one.

At 2-4, Arizona will be at home to host the Broncos in Week 7.

The 2-4 Rams are reeling and will be in Las Vegas next weekend to play the Raiders.

item.title: Liam Coen on Brian Thomas not playing in second half: Guys have to make plays
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Travis Hunter had his most productive offensive day of the season in London on Sunday and his expanded role at wide receiver came at the expense of Brian Thomas.
item.content:encoded:
Travis Hunter had his most productive offensive day of the season in London on Sunday and his expanded role at wide receiver came at the expense of Brian Thomas.

Jaguars head coach Liam Coen left Thomas on the bench for the entire second half of their 34-31 loss to the Texans. Thomas was targeted three times in the first half, but had a drop and no catches before spending the rest of the day on the sideline. Thomas also went without a catch in Week 5, which led to a question for Coen about his confidence in the 2024 first-round pick.

"Just week to week. Week to week. Guys have to step up and make plays," Coen said, via Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union.

Jaguars General Manager James Gladstone called trade chatter concerning Thomas "fraudulent" in March, but the last couple of weeks give some reason to think that conversations could be had about what whether the wideout's future is in Jacksonville.
